title: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games
abstract: arXiv:2611.18468v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The questions of voting rights, group membership, and the boundaries of acceptable discourse all involve a recursive, self-stability issue, wherein the voters, group members, and acceptable commentators are often the ultimate arbiters of their own rules for inclusion and exclusion. In order to understand how ideological or issue diversity may impact the stability of such inclusion and exclusion, we introduce franchise elections, where voting members of a group vote to change the electorate. In particular, when agents are positioned inside an ideological or issue space, a social choice function that aggregates agent viewpoints induces a preference for agents over group composition, where agents prefer groups that improve the social choice function outcome for them. We demonstrate that when ideological space is two-dimensional, these franchise elections can generate complex behavior and that this complexity exists for any social choice f

translated_title: 空间投票博弈中的选举权剥夺
translated_abstract: 关于投票权、群体成员资格以及可接受言论边界的问题都涉及一个递归的自稳定性问题，其中投票者、群体成员和可接受的评论者往往是自身包容与排斥规则的最终裁决者。为了理解意识形态或议题多样性如何影响这种包容与排斥的稳定性，我们引入了“选举权选举”，即群体的投票成员通过投票来改变选民构成。特别地，当参与者被置于意识形态或议题空间中时，聚合参与者观点的社会选择函数会诱导出参与者对群体构成的偏好，其中参与者偏好那些能为其改善社会选择函数结果的群体。我们证明，当意识形态空间是二维时，这些选举权选举可以产生复杂的行为，并且这种复杂性存在于任何社会选择函数中。
tldr: 本文提出“选举权选举”这一新模型来研究群体成员投票改变选民构成的递归自稳定问题，并证明在二维意识形态空间中此类选举会产生复杂行为，且该复杂性对任意社会选择函数均存在。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces franchise elections, where voting members vote to change the electorate, and demonstrates that in two-dimensional ideological spaces such elections generate complex behavior that exists for any social choice function.
